title: AhnLab: WinWyvern malware spread via fake Ollama site uses BYOVD to disable Korean security products
date_note: The AhnLab ASEC post gives only its own publication day; no earlier date is stated.
org: South Korean users and domestic security products (AhnLab ASEC research)
geo_basis: Country stated by the source (South Korean users and domestic security products); Seoul used as a country-level pin
summary: AhnLab's ASEC says malware called WinWyvern is spread through a Korean-language fake download site imitating the official Ollama AI tool page. According to ASEC, the installer also installs genuine Ollama components, and a malicious DLL uses the BYOVD technique with a signed anti-cheat driver to load WinWyvern. ASEC says WinWyvern patches the memory of domestic antivirus products to disable detection and blocking.
plain: AhnLab says a fake Ollama download site in Korean spreads malware that abuses a legitimate driver to switch off Korean antivirus products.
exec: AhnLab reports malware disguised as an AI tool that disables domestic security products in South Korea, which could let follow-on malware go undetected.
action: AhnLab advises caution with disguised AI tool download sites; it says the latest AhnLab V3 (Lite) is not affected by the memory patching and can detect and remove the components.

validation.note: Only AhnLab's own ASEC research post was read; no independent publisher found.

review.note: Compared title, date, BYOVD/fake Ollama site, memory patching and V3 Lite advice against the ASEC post
